name: San Sebastián
tagline: More Michelin stars per square meter than any other city on Earth — and the pintxo bar still rules.

Arzak.description: A world icon of Basque cuisine, now run by Elena Arzak. Three Michelin stars since 1989.

Akelarre.description: Views of the Cantabrian Sea and chef Pedro Subijana's cuisine, reinventing itself for half a century. Three Michelin stars.

Ganbara.description: The monkfish-and-prawn pintxo, and a bar packed with seasonal mushrooms, on Calle San Jerónimo.

La Cuchara de San Telmo.description: The pioneer of modern Basque pintxos, no sign on the door but a line at the bar.

Mugaritz.description: A 20-course tasting menu that challenges what a restaurant even is, from chef Andoni Luis Aduriz, in Errenteria.

Amelia by Paulo Airaudo.description: Seasonal cooking built on small local producers, from Italian-Argentine chef Paulo Airaudo. Two Michelin stars.

Kokotxa.description: Traditional Basque cooking brought up to date, right in the heart of the Old Town. One Michelin star.

Gandarias.description: A renovated classic: pig's ear and Idiazábal cheese risotto sit alongside the everyday pintxos.

El Tamboril.description: The most-ordered battered prawn pintxo on Calle Pescadería.

La Cepa.description: A classic Old Town bar, with a mushroom pintxo as simple as it is irresistible.

Martín Berasategui.description: The home restaurant of Martín Berasategui, the chef with more Michelin stars than anyone alive, just outside Donostia in Lasarte-Oria. Three Michelin stars since 2001.

Elkano.description: Aitor Arregi's grilled turbot in the fishing port of Getaria, a technique his father Pedro invented in 1964. Anthony Bourdain visited on 'Parts Unknown' (2017) alongside Juan Mari Arzak; one Michelin star.

Eme Be Garrote.description: Martín Berasategui's reinvented cider house in the Ibaeta area: grill, tartare, and a nod to Basque cider-house tradition. One Michelin star.

Mirador de Ulía.description: Sea-driven cooking with panoramic bay views from the slopes of Mount Ulía. One Michelin star.

Alameda.description: Third generation at the helm of a family restaurant in Hondarribia, with contemporary cooking drawn from the Bidasoa valley's pantry. One Michelin star.

Narru.description: Contemporary market-driven Basque cooking across from the Buen Pastor Cathedral; the name honors the chef's great-grandfather, a professional pelota player.

Rekondo.description: A classic Basque grill house since 1964 on the road up Mount Igeldo, with one of the most admired wine cellars in the world.

Bodegón Alejandro.description: Seasonal Basque cooking, game, and fish, in an understated dining room in the heart of the Old Town, sourced from small local producers.

Astelena 1997.description: A hake puff-pastry pie made from a family recipe, served in a former banana warehouse turned high-ceilinged dining room.

Zazpi Taberna.description: Chef Paul Arrillaga's gastro-bar, serving product-driven Basque cooking with contemporary technique near the Boulevard.

Topa Sukalderia.description: Basque-Latin American fusion devised by Andoni Luis Aduriz of Mugaritz, steps from Zurriola beach.

Branka.description: A terrace beside Chillida's Peine del Viento sculpture on Ondarreta beach, serving traditional, market-driven cooking.

La Perla.description: A century-old restaurant and bathhouse overlooking La Concha beach, with views across the whole bay from its terraces.

Kaia-Kaipe.description: Facing Getaria's fishing port since 1962: fish grilled over coals, turbot, and its own live shellfish tank.

Casa Urola.description: A bar of classic and modern pintxos plus an upstairs dining room with a market menu, on Fermín Calbetón street. Bib Gourmand.

Borda Berri.description: Wine-braised veal cheek and roasted pig's ear, cooked to order at one of the most acclaimed bars in the Old Town. No reservations.

Bar Nestor.description: Just two potato tortillas made per day and a tomato salad that sells out in minutes, running since 1980. No reservations — arrive early.

Txepetxa.description: Specialists in vinegar-cured anchovies since 1972, with a dozen possible toppings for each pintxo.

Bar Zeruko.description: The most avant-garde bar in the Old Town: smoke, foams, and cod smoked right at the counter.

Sirimiri.description: Fusion pintxos and a cocktail list built heavily around vermouth, right by the Santa María church.

Casa Alcalde.description: Acorn-fed Iberian ham and grilled lamb chops, amid bullfighting posters, across from the Santa María church.

Casa Vergara 1948.description: Cod in every form — omelette, battered, skewered — since 1948, facing the Basílica de Santa María.

Aloña Berri.description: A benchmark for chef-driven pintxos in Gros since the 1990s, famous for its 'squid in balance.' Winner of San Sebastián's pintxo championship.

Bergara.description: Home of award-winning pintxos like the Txalupa and the Udaberri, in the Gros district. A Michelin Guide selection.

Bodega Donostiarra.description: A neighborhood institution on Fermín Calbetón, known for tinned seafood, octopus, and grilled meat.

La Viña.description: Birthplace, in 1990, of the burnt Basque cheesecake that has since conquered the world — caramelized outside, molten within.

Churrería Santa Lucía.description: Churros and hot chocolate since 1957, next to Plaza de la Constitución, with wooden benches and an old-world feel.

Petritegi Sagardotegia.description: A cider-making farmhouse dating to 1526 in Astigarraga: rib steak, omelette, and cider straight from the barrel during txotx season.

Mercado de la Bretxa.description: A covered market dating to 1870 in the heart of the Old Town, with fishmongers, butchers, and long-standing stalls.

Mercado de San Martín.description: Donostia's liveliest market: fruit, vegetables, fresh fish straight from the auction, and bread, right in the city center.
